hypothesis: Replace coupled detailed-route history search with a weighted decision diagram whose state is the exact compatibility interface visible to remaining pair tasks.
mechanism: Independently generate a finite route domain for each original pair using static unbiased, preferred-layer and four spatially biased shortest-path profiles. Freeze every domain before coupled search. Selecting a route projects its exact geometric compatibility into one allowed-choice mask per future task. Histories with identical future masks have identical feasible suffix assignments, so retain only the cheaper exact backpointer witness. This is a future-extension quotient, not a memo of completed task names.
proof_assumptions: All future task domains and their binary compatibility relation remain immutable for the entire diagram. No prefix witness, forgotten drill history or selected route generates future columns after merging. The fixed task index retains pair identity and endpoints separately from root ownership. Ordered route vertices, layers, trace widths, full-span via copper and owner-independent drill resources determine compatibility. Equivalent masks are local to one immutable instance and never shared between different rule/geometry contexts.
exactness: The decision diagram preserves feasibility and minimum base route cost within the frozen finite domains. Costs are not the biased profile costs; witnesses keep their actual graph edge costs. Exact interface merges may drop a more expensive equivalent prefix. There is no approximate frontier trimming. Empty domains, finite-family incompatibility, a state cap or a work limit remain unknown for the continuous board and create no upstream exclusion.
domain: Ordinary unscaled Pipeline9 nodes with two to twelve pair tasks whose finite endpoints lie inside the prototype node/layer domain. Graph wires use endpoint-aligned/uniform coordinates and exact endpoint chords; vias use interior through-via sites. Static profile enumeration is incomplete and can omit required detours or shared drill choices. Native candidates retain their original effort and expansion budgets.
physical_contract: All accepted routes preserve exact pair endpoints, root aliases and regionId. Copper compatibility uses actual requested widths and full-stack via barrels. Same-net copper sharing does not erase distinct drill-site spacing; exact shared sites are reusable. The actual caller hole diameter and minimum hole-edge gap are propagated into generation, compatibility, conversion and final validation. Within-task drills, pads, fixed obstacles and the real board are independently validated before publication; rejected geometry never creates a learned fact.
budgets_and_scheduling: Domain construction and diagram work share 40000 times pair count times effort engine steps. Maximum exact frontier width is 4096 states per layer. The candidate batches 64 engine steps per portfolio call; fitness uses actual engine work and all original candidates retain their budgets/expansion clock. This scheduling choice must be included in fidelity review; activation is not timing evidence.
setup_costs: Candidate constructor ownership/obstacle preparation, graph allocation, all independent profile searches, frozen-domain copying, compatibility projection and losing-candidate work must all be counted. They occur during ordinary high-density execution. Seven profiles on a two-layer node can cost more than a successful native route even if the diagram is small. End-to-end paired Blacksmith elapsed is the performance measure.
positive_evidence: 128 randomized finite route families match exhaustive assignment feasibility and minimum base cost, including multiple pairs sharing root labels
8^8 independent route histories compress to one state per layer and 64 transitions while reconstructing all eight exact cheapest pair witnesses
A boundary test proves all domains are frozen before the diagram's first step and no further domain query or generation occurs during coupled search
State/work cap tests preserve an available finite-family solution as unknown instead of dropping a distinguishable state
Default ordinary P9 fixture reaches frozen-domain projection and executes DD transitions
Physical crossings, mandatory layer transitions, rotated obstacles, full-span barrels, board/pad validation, exact same-site drill reuse and actual caller drill-rule propagation
Overhang eligibility, regionId, within-task drill rejection, async routes/stats and native portfolio work-clock regressions
controlled_negative: Two same-net via pairs in a 2mm square can require moving to legal shared or farther drill sites, yet static shortest-path profiles may generate only their individually shortest too-close sites. The exact diagram correctly rejects that finite family as unknown although a physical board solution exists. The smaller single-site fixture proves legal sharing is retained. This is a route-domain limitation, not an interface-equivalence failure.
telemetry: Phase stats separate domain queries/vertex expansions, generated/duplicate/self-invalid choices, frozen-domain activations, exact compatibility projections, attempted/incompatible transitions, unique/stored states, merged/dominated histories, cheaper-witness replacements, maximum state width and affected future tasks, physical validation/rejection and each unknown cap exit.
falsifiers: Domain construction dominates removed coupled-search work
Few real histories merge or frontier width rapidly reaches its cap
Frozen route domains omit the needed topology or legal drill choices too often
Default activation produces little accepted work or a full-board physical quality regression
Audited paired end-to-end improvement remains far below the proposed breakthrough scale
performance_claim: None before audited paired Blacksmith results. The synthetic history count is a representation proof, not an estimate of real-board CPU savings. Results apply to this fixed-domain weighted compatibility diagram, not an unrestricted low-treewidth PCB solver.
